description: Verify that DUT TCP includes exponential (more than linear) backoff for successive RTO values for data segments (RFC 1122 §4.2.3.1, RFC 6298 §5)
approach:
[Objective]
Exponential RTO backoff for data: each successive retx interval > previous (geometric, not arithmetic). Protects from triangle-of-thrash when the peer is unreachable.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Handshake → DUT sends data → tester drops all retransmits.
2. DUT → Tester: data, retx_1, retx_2, retx_3.
3. Observation: Δt(retx_2) > Δt(retx_1); Δt(retx_3) > Δt(retx_2).

[Pass condition]
Intervals strictly grow.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_seg1 — initial data missing
• Fail_no_retx_<n> — retransmit n missing
• Fail_initial_rto_out_of_window — first retx interval out of baseline
• Fail_retx<n>_not_doubled — interval n not larger than n-1

verdicts.Fail_initial_rto_out_of_window: Data retx 1 RTO out of baseline window
verdicts.Fail_retx2_not_doubled: Data retx 2 delta not greater than initial RTO
verdicts.Fail_retx3_not_doubled: Data retx 3 delta not greater than retx 2 lower bound
